title: From a question to an executed numerical workflow

attempts.prompt: Use the simulated PenSim demo case NC-03ce17b48c95. At 60 h, air is limited to 1.0x. Compare the current operating plan with the permitted alternatives for the rest of the batch. Show simulated penicillin and dissolved oxygen, identify constraint violations, and recommend a plan for human review. Clearly label simulated predictions and uncertainty; do not claim actual manufacturing savings or execute equipment changes.
attempts.reply:
Understood. This is a simulated what-if on the public PenSim challenge case NC-03ce17b48c95 (industrial penicillin fed-batch, operating change chosen part-way through the batch), with air limited to 1.0x at the 60 h decision point. Everything that follows is a simulated prediction offered for human review - not plant data, and nothing here executes or authorizes any equipment change.

What I am setting up:
1. bioprocess_demo_case loads case NC-03ce17b48c95 to show its observed history and stated operating limits, and to confirm the scenario matches your description (decision at 60 h, air at 1.0x).
2. bioprocess_forecast then runs all six permitted non-abstain plans: keep (current plan), lean, standard, rich, lean_low_gas, standard_low_gas. Ranking objective: highest simulated penicillin P (g/L) over the remainder of the batch while dissolved oxygen DO2 (mg/L) and the other stated limits stay satisfied. For each plan I will report P and DO2 at target times with units, feasibility, and any violated limits.

Caveats to weigh when the results attach:
- Simulated case: the forecasting tool and the case come from the same simulator family and share equations and the fitted source batch, so close agreement is expected and is not validation.
- The calibrated model is qualified for the 96 h window only; the full 230 h batch is not offered.
- Fitted growth, kLa and production factors are effective values; 15 of 48 experiment fits sat near a parameter bound.
- In the final A/B experiment the tool cut PenSim forecast error by 16.5% (95% interval -0.3 to 30.4), short of the 20% bar and with an interval spanning zero - so treat point forecasts as approximate and compare plans by margins and direction, not decimals.
- The demo packet contains the observed history only; evaluator outcomes are not included, so the ranking rests entirely on the simulated forecasts.
- Environment flag: the model registry currently lists the PenSim simulator environment as not installed (missing /tmp/biodemo/simulators/... paths). If the run returns an error, that environment needs to be installed by the platform team; I cannot install it myself.

Once results attach, I will give a clearly labeled comparison of P and DO2 per plan, list any constraint violations, and recommend a plan for human review - with no claim of actual manufacturing savings.

attempts.prompt: Please run only the standard freeze-drying demo with the registered lyo.kv_rp model. Use its default assumptions. Show the numerical results and limitations. Do not request an agent interpretation or any equipment action.
attempts.reply:
Understood — I'll run only the standard freeze-drying demo with the registered lyo.kv_rp model, under its default assumptions, with no interpretation request and no equipment action.

What I'm submitting:
1. Load the standard demo context (technology-transfer example). This is the published/reconstructed demo; its observations are synthetic reconstructions, not plant data, and I will keep them clearly labeled as such.
2. Prepare a single-model pipeline using only lyo.kv_rp (quasi-steady Kv–Rp, unqualified engineering demonstration). Defaults throughout: no calibration, default evidence cutoff (6 h), interface-temperature observable, 4 samples, seed 2025, capped at 32 solver calls and 30 s wall time. This model has no required thermal inputs, so no thermal assumptions are invented; note it inherently neglects sensible-heat dynamics. I'll request the trajectories and validation views so temperatures and drying progress can be shown next to the demo's held-out synthetic observations.
3. Execute the plan — the UI will attach the actual numerical results, so I won't quote numbers before they exist.

Once the results attach, I'll report the interface and bottom temperatures (°C), remaining ice per vial, sublimation rate, drying time and constraint margins, together with the limitations that matter here: representative-vial resolution (cannot establish hottest-vial protection), prescribed chamber pressure becoming invalid above the equipment's vapor-handling capacity, neglected sensible-heat dynamics, unqualified engineering-demonstration status, and reconstructed/synthetic observations rather than measured plant data. Numerical completion is not residual moisture, potency or release suitability. No equipment changes will be proposed or executed; any follow-up would go to human review only.
